quarterly_data.signal: Credo's 10-K describes a fabless model: in fiscal year 2026 Credo exclusively used TSMC for semiconductor wafer production and outsources all of its IC manufacturing to TSMC; after wafer fabrication it uses third-party contractors Amkor Technology and Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) for packaging its IC products, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC) and Sigurd Microelectronics for testing its IC products, and BizLink Technology for manufacturing its AEC products. Except for its agreement with BizLink for the manufacture of certain AEC products, Credo does not maintain long-term supply contracts with TSMC or its other contract manufacturers or suppliers; none of TSMC, BizLink or its other manufacturers or suppliers has provided contractual capacity assurances, and Credo has not entered capacity commitment arrangements with TSMC. It expects a transition to new foundry or assembly providers would take approximately 9 to 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 9 to 12 months to transition foundry or assembly services to new providers

quarterly_data.signal: Credo's 10-K: as of May 2, 2026 it had three manufacturing supply capacity reservation agreements with assembly subcontractors (remaining terms of two to five years), paying refundable deposits for reserved production capacity and committing to purchase levels of at least $188.6 million for fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2028; refundable deposits were $71.0 million. Non-cancelable inventory purchase orders with foundry partners and subcontractors payable within one year were approximately $149.2 million. After May 2, 2026 Credo entered another capacity reservation agreement with an assembly subcontractor, paying $13.1 million of refundable deposits with approximately $43.7 million of inventory purchases committed over the next two years. Fiscal 2026 inventory rose $174.0 million to support unfulfilled backlog and new product ramps; remaining performance obligations were approximately $31.9 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 capacity reservation agreements; purchase commitments at least $188.6 million (FY2027-FY2028); refundable deposits $71.0 million; new agreement $13.1 million deposits, $43.7 million committed purchases; non-cancelable purchase orders ~$149.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: Credo's 10-K: in fiscal year 2022 Credo issued Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC a warrant (the Customer Warrant) to purchase up to 4.1 million ordinary shares, vesting in tranches based on the amount of global payments by the holder and its affiliates to Credo, up to $201.0 million in aggregate payments; the related expense is amortized as a reduction of revenue in proportion to the related revenue recognized. A total of 4.1 million Customer Warrant shares had vested as of May 3, 2025, and the holder had exercised all of them as of May 2, 2026. The filing does not name the products Amazon purchases.
quarterly_data.figure: Customer Warrant vesting tied to up to $201.0 million of aggregate payments; 4.1 million shares vested as of May 3, 2025
